key_insight: Synthetic crystal structures can support diffusion pretraining for materials property prediction while reducing reliance on costly DFT-relaxed training structures.
engineering_relevance: Fast machine-learned relaxation offers a practical route to larger, more structurally diverse pretraining datasets without new DFT calculations for every generated crystal.
method: Generate synthetic crystals through perturb-and-relax, MatterGen sampling, and protostructure enumeration.
Use machine-learned interatomic potentials where structural relaxation is needed.
Pretrain a randomly initialized Orb-v2 backbone using coordinate denoising or continuous-time VP and sub-VP diffusion objectives.
evidence_signal: Every synthetic-pretraining condition numerically outperformed random initialization across seven MatBench tasks; scaling protostructures from 20k to 165k matched or exceeded MP-20k pretraining on most tasks in an eight-task study.
watch_item: The fixed 400-epoch scaling protocol increases both dataset diversity and optimization updates, so gains cannot be attributed to data scale alone.
paper_title: Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction
